perf.summary: Hoist the n*m (n*n) loop-bound product out of the for-condition so it is computed once instead of every iteration.
perf.currentCost: The loop condition i < n * m re-evaluates an integer multiply on every iteration (n*m extra IMUL + compare per element across all four element-wise kernels).
perf.proposedChange: int total = n * m; for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) ... ; likewise int total = n * n; in RunSquare.
perf.rationale: The product is loop-invariant. Computing it once removes one multiply from the per-iteration dependency/instruction stream. Burst/LLVM often hoists this, but making it explicit guarantees it and shortens the trip-count expression so the vectorizer sees a clean affine bound, improving auto-vectorization of these trivially SIMD-able zero/add/sub loops.
perf.risk: None. Pure loop-invariant code motion; n*m overflow behavior is identical since the same product is what indexes a[i] today. Same observable output.

perf.summary: Zero-fill via a byte memory clear (Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned) instead of a scalar element store loop.
perf.currentCost: Per-element scalar store of 0L over n*m longs; relies on the JIT/Burst to recognize and widen the memset pattern, which it may not always do for raw pointer loops.
perf.rationale: InitBlockUnaligned lowers to a single optimized memset / vectorized clear, moving far more bytes per instruction than a long-at-a-time store loop and eliminating the loop overhead entirely. Burst supports Unsafe.InitBlock intrinsics.
perf.risk: Byte count (n*m)*8 must not overflow uint; for matrix sizes this holds but guard if n*m can exceed ~2^29 longs. Zeroing all-bits-0 equals 0L for two's-complement long, so semantics are identical.

perf.summary: Replace the O(n^2) per-element (i==j) branch with an O(n^2) zero-fill followed by an O(n) diagonal write.
perf.currentCost: n*n iterations each doing an index multiply i*n+j and a conditional select (i==j)?1:0; the branch/select and the inner multiply run for every cell even though only n cells are nonzero.
perf.proposedChange: Zero the whole buffer (InitBlockUnaligned or the hoisted-bound loop), then for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) a[i * n + i] = 1; The diagonal index i*n+i can be carried as a running offset (idx += n + 1) to drop the multiply.
perf.rationale: The bulk zeroing becomes a memset/vectorizable pass with no per-cell branch, and only n diagonal stores remain. This removes n*n-n redundant branches/selects and replaces n inner multiplies with additions. Same asymptotic class but a much smaller constant and SIMD-friendly.
perf.risk: None. Output identical: off-diagonal zeros, diagonal ones. The running-offset trick is exact for the affine index i*(n+1).

perf.summary: Reorder loops to i-k-j (or transpose b) so the inner loop streams b row-contiguously instead of striding by p, and hoist row base pointers.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop reads b[k * p + j] which strides by p elements (p*8 bytes) per k step: a cache miss / TLB-unfriendly column walk, and recomputes i*m+k and k*p+j multiplies each inner iteration. For large matrices this column traversal dominates cost via cache misses.
perf.proposedChange: Swap to the i-k-j order: zero c first, then for i, for k { long aik = a[i*m+k]; long* brow = b + k*p; long* crow = c + i*p; for j: crow[j] += aik * brow[j]; }. Both a and b are now accessed contiguously in the inner loop, and a[i*m+k] is hoisted out of the j-loop. Row base pointers replace the per-iteration index multiplies with pointer adds.
perf.rationale: i-k-j makes every inner-loop access unit-stride, which is what Burst/LLVM auto-vectorizes (FMA over crow[j] += aik*brow[j]) and what the hardware prefetcher loves; the original i-j-k inner loop over b is column-major and defeats both. Hoisting aik and the row pointers removes p multiplies and a load from the inner loop. This is the single biggest win in the file for non-trivial n,m,p.
perf.risk: Semantics-preserving for integer long arithmetic (integer add/mul are associative/commutative, and i-k-j accumulates the same products into c[i*p+j]); requires c be zeroed first since accumulation is now incremental. Wrapping/overflow result is bit-identical because each c[i,j] still sums exactly the same set of products. Slightly more memory traffic on c (read-modify-write) but cache-resident per row.

perf.summary: Skip the final redundant squaring of a, and replace the result/a copy-back loops with pointer swaps.
perf.currentCost: Each while iteration unconditionally squares a (MatrixMul over n^3) AND copies temp->a over n*n, even on the last iteration where exp becomes 0 and the squared a is never used again — a wasted O(n^3) multiply plus O(n^2) copy. The two copy-back loops also move n*n longs each iteration instead of swapping buffers.
perf.proposedChange: Guard the squaring: only square a when exp > 1 after the shift (i.e. compute exp >>= 1 first, then if (exp > 0) square). Replace 'MatrixMul into temp then copy temp back into result/a' with computing into temp and swapping the pointers (long* tmpPtr = result; result = temp; temp = tmpPtr;), so no O(n^2) copy is needed per multiply.
perf.rationale: Eliminates one full n^3 matrix multiply plus an n^2 copy on the final loop iteration, and removes up to 2 n^2 element copies per iteration by swapping pointers instead. For exp with B bits this saves ~B copies of n^2 longs. Pointer swap is O(1).
perf.risk: Caller passes result/a/temp as distinct buffers; swapping result/temp pointers means the final answer may end up in the buffer originally named temp. Must ensure the routine copies the final result back into the caller-provided result buffer (one final O(n^2) copy if the parity left it in temp) or document which buffer holds the output. The skip-final-square guard is exact: when exp becomes 0 the squared a is provably dead.

perf.summary: Hoist the row base pointer (a + i*m) out of the inner loop to strength-reduce the i*m+j index multiply into a pointer add.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop computes a[i*m+j]: an i*m multiply (loop-invariant for the inner loop) plus +j each iteration. The i*m product is recomputed for every j.
perf.proposedChange: long* arow = a + i * m; then inner: sum += arow[j] * v[j];. Same pattern applies to MatrixMul's a-row.
perf.rationale: Lifts the invariant i*m out of the j-loop and turns the address computation into arow + j (single add / base+index addressing), shortening the per-iteration dependency chain and helping the vectorizer treat arow[j]*v[j] as a clean dot-product reduction.
perf.risk: None. Pure loop-invariant code motion; identical addresses and results.

perf.summary: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to the hot leaf kernels (especially MatrixMul.Run and the copy/zero helpers called by MatrixPow).
perf.currentCost: MatrixPow calls MatrixMul.Run repeatedly across a call boundary; without inlining hints Burst may keep them as separate functions, preventing cross-call constant propagation of n and loop fusion.
perf.proposedChange: Annotate the small element-wise kernels and MatrixMul.Run with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] (the using for System.Runtime.CompilerServices is already present).
perf.rationale: Inlining MatrixMul into MatrixPow lets Burst propagate that all three dimensions equal n (square case), specialize the loop bounds, and potentially fuse the multiply with the subsequent copy/swap, reducing call overhead and enabling better register allocation.
perf.risk: Inlining a triple-nested loop can increase code size / I-cache pressure; apply selectively. Behavior is unchanged. On mobile, weigh code-size growth — mark only the genuinely hot, small kernels.
